$comment: Paket FK, Aufgabenform B2 „Welche Fassung schickst du?“: zwei Fassungen (`good` richtig, `bad` mit dem typischen Fehler), Begründung, danach ein neuer Satz mit zwei Stellen (`next.s` mit {1} und {2}; je Stelle zwei Optionen, `ok` = Index der richtigen). Gegenlesung durch den english-teacher vor dem Test-Link.

sit.de: Du schreibst einem Kunden, der seit Tagen nicht antwortet.
sit.en: You write to a customer who has not replied for days.

tasks.good: I haven't heard from you since Monday.
tasks.bad: I didn't hear from you since Monday.

why.de: „Since Monday“ reicht bis jetzt, also Present Perfect: „haven't heard“. Das Past Simple passt nur zu einer abgeschlossenen Zeit.
why.en: “Since Monday” reaches up to now, so it takes the Present Perfect: “haven't heard”. The Past Simple only fits a finished time.

next.s: We {1} on this ticket {2} two days.

sit.de: Du schreibst der Geschäftsführung einen Kurzbericht über einen Ausfall.
sit.en: You write a short report to the management about an outage.

tasks.good: Over 200 customers were affected by the outage last month.
tasks.bad: Over 200 customers are affected by the outage last month.

why.de: „Last month“ liegt in der Vergangenheit, also steht das Passiv im Past Simple: „were affected“.
why.en: “Last month” is in the past, so the passive takes the Past Simple: “were affected”.

next.s: The server {1} yesterday, and the data {2} within an hour.

sit.de: Du erklärst deiner Chefin, was du mit mehr Budget tun würdest.
sit.en: You tell your manager what you would do with a bigger budget.

tasks.good: If I had more budget, I would hire another developer.
tasks.bad: If I would have more budget, I would hire another developer.

why.de: Im „if“-Satz einer unwahrscheinlichen Annahme steht das Past Simple („had“). „Would“ gehört nur in den Hauptsatz.
why.en: In the “if” clause of an unlikely situation the Past Simple is used (“had”). “Would” belongs only in the main clause.

next.s: If the customer {1} sooner, we {2} the contract this week.

sit.de: Du bittest einen erfahrenen Kollegen um Rat zu einem Vertrag.
sit.en: You ask an experienced colleague for advice on a contract.

tasks.good: Could you give me some advice on this contract?
tasks.bad: Could you give me an advice on this contract?

why.de: „Advice“ ist nicht zählbar: kein „an“, keine Mehrzahl. Man sagt „some advice“.
why.en: “Advice” is uncountable: no “an”, no plural. You say “some advice”.

next.s: Thanks for the {1}. The {2} in your email was very helpful.

sit.de: Du gibst eine Aussage der Kundin an deinen Chef weiter.
sit.en: You pass a customer's statement on to your boss.

tasks.good: She told me that she had already sent the invoice.
tasks.bad: She told that she had already sent the invoice.

why.de: „Tell“ braucht direkt eine Person („told me“). Ohne Person sagt man „said“.
why.en: “Tell” needs a person right after it (“told me”). Without a person you say “said”.

next.s: He {1} me he {2} the file the next day.

sit.de: Du berichtest von einem Terminvorschlag deines Kollegen.
sit.en: You report a colleague's suggestion for a meeting.

tasks.good: He suggested meeting at the office.
tasks.bad: He suggested to meet at the office.

why.de: Nach „suggest“ folgt die -ing-Form oder ein „that“-Satz, nicht „to“ + Grundform.
why.en: “Suggest” is followed by the -ing form or a “that” clause, not “to” + base form.

next.s: I look forward to {1} you, and I enjoy {2} with your team.

sit.de: Du erzählst, wie es dir mit der neuen Spesen-Software ging.
sit.en: You say how it went with the new expense software.

tasks.good: It took me weeks to get used to the new expense system.
tasks.bad: It took me weeks to be used to the new expense system.

why.de: „Get used to“ ist der Vorgang des Gewöhnens (das dauerte Wochen). „Be used to“ ist der Zustand, schon gewohnt zu sein.
why.en: “Get used to” is the process of becoming accustomed (it took weeks). “Be used to” is the state of already being accustomed.

next.s: I {1} use the old tool every day, so I'm still getting used to {2} the new one.

sit.de: Du planst die Migration der Archive.
sit.en: You plan the migration of the archives.

tasks.good: By next spring, we will have migrated all archives.
tasks.bad: By next spring, we will migrated all archives.

why.de: Bis zu einem künftigen Zeitpunkt abgeschlossen: Future Perfect, „will have“ + Partizip.
why.en: Finished by a future point: Future Perfect, “will have” + past participle.

next.s: By Friday, I {1} the report, and by Monday we {2} the data.

sit.de: Du schließt eine Mail an einen Kunden ab.
sit.en: You close an email to a customer.

tasks.good: I'm looking forward to your reply.
tasks.bad: I'm looking forward for your reply.

why.en: The phrase is “look forward to”, not “for”.

next.s: Can you explain {1} how the tool works, and can I share the numbers {2} you?

sit.de: Du bittest per Mail um die Dokumenttypen.
sit.en: You ask for the document types by email.

tasks.good: The list of document types is needed by Friday.
tasks.bad: The list of document types are needed by Friday.

why.de: Das Verb richtet sich nach „the list“ (Einzahl), nicht nach „document types“.
why.en: The verb agrees with “the list” (singular), not with “document types”.

next.s: The news {1} good, and the next steps {2} clear.

sit.de: Du erklärst, warum das Update zu spät kam.
sit.en: You explain why the update was late.

tasks.good: Delayed by a server outage, the update went live late.
tasks.bad: Delaying by a server outage, the update went live late.

why.de: Das Update wurde verzögert: passive Bedeutung, also das Partizip Perfekt („delayed“).
why.en: The update was delayed: passive meaning, so the past participle (“delayed”).

next.s: {1} the proposal, she sent it to the board. {2} by the budget, they postponed the launch.

sit.de: Du blickst auf ein verspätetes Projekt zurück.
sit.en: You look back on a late project.

tasks.good: I wish we had hired a second developer earlier.
tasks.bad: I wish we would have hired a second developer earlier.

why.de: Bedauern über die Vergangenheit: „wish“ + Past Perfect. „Would have“ hört man in den USA umgangssprachlich, im Geschäftsenglisch gilt es als falsch.
why.en: Regret about the past: “wish” + Past Perfect. “Would have” is heard in casual American speech, but in business English it counts as wrong.

next.s: I wish the migration {1} already finished, and I wish we {2} the plan last year.

sit.de: Du suchst im Team nach der Ursache eines Fehlers.
sit.en: You look for the cause of a bug with the team.

tasks.good: Sven can't have caused this error; he was on vacation.
tasks.bad: Sven can't cause this error; he was on vacation.

why.de: Eine sichere Folgerung über die Vergangenheit braucht „couldn't have“ oder „can't have“ + Partizip („caused“). „Can't cause“ spricht über jetzt oder allgemein, nicht über gestern.
why.en: A confident deduction about the past needs “couldn't have” or “can't have” + past participle (“caused”). “Can't cause” talks about now or in general, not about yesterday.

next.s: The logs show a login at 3 a.m., so someone {1} the file, but it {2} Sven: he was on a flight.

sit.de: Du fragst beim Support nach dem Stand.
sit.en: You ask support for a status update.

tasks.good: We have been waiting for an answer for three hours.
tasks.bad: We are waiting for an answer since three hours.

why.de: Eine Tätigkeit von früher bis jetzt braucht das Present Perfect Continuous. Die Länge der Zeit bekommt „for“.
why.en: An activity from earlier until now needs the Present Perfect Continuous. A length of time takes “for”.

sit.de: Du sagst einem Kunden zu, sich zu melden.
sit.en: You promise a customer to get in touch.

tasks.good: I'll call you as soon as the update is finished.
tasks.bad: I'll call you as soon as the update will be finished.

why.de: Nach „as soon as“ steht für die Zukunft das Present, nicht „will be“.
why.en: After “as soon as” the present tense refers to the future, not “will be”.

next.s: When the customer {1}, we {2} the invoice.

sit.de: Du stellst einen Bericht im Meeting vor.
sit.en: You present a report in a meeting.

tasks.good: The report was written by our analyst.
tasks.bad: The report was written from our analyst.

why.de: Im Passiv wird der Handelnde mit „by“ angeschlossen.
why.en: In a passive sentence the doer is introduced with “by”.

next.s: The contract {1} by both teams and {2} to the customer.
